cues: Kirchhoff's junction law conserves charge, and his loop law conserves energy.
A balanced Wheatstone bridge gives P over Q equals R over S, and the metre bridge gives X equals R l over one hundred minus l.
A potentiometer draws no current at balance, so it compares e m fs and finds internal resistance exactly.
A superconductor has zero resistance and expels magnetic flux.
A shunt in parallel makes an ammeter, a multiplier in series makes a voltmeter.
And Joule's law says the heat is I squared R t.
text: Let us recap. Kirchhoff's junction law conserves charge, and his loop law conserves energy. A balanced Wheatstone bridge gives P over Q equals R over S, and the metre bridge gives X equals R l over one hundred minus l. A potentiometer draws no current at balance, so it compares e m fs and finds internal resistance exactly. A superconductor has zero resistance and expels magnetic flux. A shunt in parallel makes an ammeter, a multiplier in series makes a voltmeter. And Joule's law says the heat is I squared R t.
